name: Carbyne

summary.text: Carbyne is an emergency-communications software company, incorporated in Israel in 2014 as Reporty Homeland Security Ltd. and rebranded as Carbyne in early 2018. Its APEX platform handles 911 calls for U.S. public-safety answering points. Investors named by the company and the press include Founders Fund, Elsted Capital Partners, FinTLV and AT&T's venture arm. Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak invested in 2015 and chairs its board; former Unit 8200 director Pinhas Buchris sits on the board.

facts.claim: Haaretz reported in July 2019 that a large part of the money Ehud Barak's limited partnership Sum (E.B.) 2015 used to buy stock in Reporty (now Carbyne) was supplied by Jeffrey Epstein. Barak said a firm linked to Epstein was a passive investor and that he was looking to remove it from the partnership.
facts.quote: A large part of the money used by Sum to buy Reporty stock was supplied by Epstein, Haaretz reported Thursday.

facts.claim: Calcalist reported that Carbyne was raising a $100 million round led by AT&T's venture arm, and listed Elsted Capital Partners, FinTLV, Founders Fund and former CIA director David Petraeus among its investors.

facts.claim: Carbyne's APEX 911 call-handling platform has been adopted by U.S. public-safety agencies including Grant County, Washington's Multi Agency Communications Center (announced December 2023 as the first in Washington state), Charleston County, South Carolina (March 2025) and the Tularosa Basin Regional Dispatch Authority in Alamogordo, New Mexico (March 2025), according to the company's press releases and trade coverage.
facts.quote: the Charleston County Consolidated Emergency Communications Center has selected Carbyne's APEX platform for its 911 services

facts.claim: Urgent Communications reported that a 911 center in the New Orleans area signed a multiyear deal to replace its call-handling system with Carbyne APEX; Carbyne says APEX is hosted on AWS GovCloud and Microsoft Azure.
facts.quote: Carbyne's APEX is hosted on AWS GovCloud and Microsoft Azure

openQuestions: Wikipedia gives April 2015 as the founding date; Calcalist gives 2014 (incorporation as Reporty Homeland Security Ltd.). The owner may want to check the Israeli company registry.
Contract values and terms for the U.S. 911 deployments are not disclosed in the press releases; county procurement records would have them.
Whether the Epstein-linked firm was actually removed from Sum (E.B.) 2015 after July 2019 is not confirmed by the sources found.
